tracks.story: A temporary street circuit through Adelaide's East Parklands, rebuilt every year. It hosted eleven Formula One Australian Grands Prix from 1985 to 1995, and Supercars have raced the 3.2 km, 14-turn layout since 1999. The opening chicane is named for Ayrton Senna.
Built in seven months and opened in November 2008, laid over the Algarve hills with drops of up to 12%. Formula 1 came in 2020 for the first Portuguese GP in 24 years.

heritage.Torre VIP: TORRE VIP · UNDER THE VIP TOWER
heritage.Galp: GALP · DROP ONTO THE MAIN STRAIGHT

tracks.story: Opened in 1960 as Atlanta International Raceway, south of Atlanta. Bruton Smith bought it in 1990 and added a road course that first raced in 1992, mixing the oval with an infield section. Renamed EchoPark Speedway in 2025.

Built by Roger Penske on the site of the old Kaiser Steel mill in Fontana, opened in June 1997. The Kaiser water tower was kept in the infield as a scoreboard. Gil de Ferran's 241.428 mph pole lap in 2000 set the closed-course speed record.

tracks.display: Autodromo Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari
tracks.story: Inaugurated on 25 April 1953 beside the Santerno river, Imola was built on design hints from Enzo Ferrari and now carries his name and that of his son Dino. It runs anti-clockwise through the hills. The 1994 San Marino Grand Prix weekend took Roland Ratzenberger and Ayrton Senna, and Tamburello became a chicane.

heritage.Tamburello: ONCE FLAT OUT · MADE A CHICANE AFTER 1994
heritage.Variante Villeneuve: FOR GILLES VILLENEUVE · HIS 1980 CRASH SITE
heritage.Acque Minerali: FOR THE PARK OF THE MINERAL WATERS

tracks.story: Opened in 1959 in Mexico City's Magdalena Mixhuca park, 2,238 m above sea level, and named for the racing brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez. The lap ends through the Foro Sol, a ballpark built inside the old Peraltada.

Tuscan road races ran through Mugello from the 1920s until 1970. The closed circuit opened in 1974 and has been owned by Ferrari since 1988; F1 came for the 2020 Tuscan GP. Two corners honour local heroes Materassi and Biondetti.

heritage.San Donato: SAN DONATO · A BISHOP OF FIESOLE
heritage.Borgo San Lorenzo: BORGO SAN LORENZO · THE NEARBY TOWN
heritage.Main straight: 1.141 KM FLAT OUT TO SAN DONATO

tracks.story: Inaugurated on 12 May 1940 between the Guarapiranga and Billings lakes, which gives Interlagos its name. Renamed in 1985 for José Carlos Pace, who won his only Grand Prix here in 1975, it runs anti-clockwise with the Senna S at Turn 1.

heritage.Reta dos Boxes: THE START IS IN THE TRIBUNAS

tracks.story: Built in 1922 in the wooded park of the Royal Villa of Monza. The Temple of Speed: long straights and fast corners, broken up by chicanes, with the old banked oval still standing beside it.
George Barber built the park in 2003 on 880 acres outside Birmingham, beside his vintage motorsport museum. Its gardens and sculptures earned it the nickname 'The Augusta National of Motorsports'.

heritage.Charlotte's Web: FOR THE GIANT STEEL SPIDER IN THE INFIELD

tracks.display: Detroit Grand Prix at Belle Isle
tracks.story: From 1992 to 2022 the Detroit Grand Prix ran on Belle Isle, a 982-acre island park in the Detroit River shaped by Frederick Law Olmsted, with the Renaissance Center skyline on one side and Canada on the other. Roger Penske revived the race in 2007 and again in 2012, and the event funded millions in park repairs, including the Scott Fountain.

heritage.Back straight: ALONG THE DETROIT RIVER · NEAR 170 MPH

tracks.story: Opened in 1950 in a natural amphitheatre in Kent, the first purpose-built post-war circuit in England. The short Indy loop sits in the bowl; the Grand Prix loop runs out through Westfield Wood.

heritage.Paddock Hill Bend: NAMED FOR THE PITS AND PADDOCK BESIDE IT
heritage.Graham Hill Bend: GRAHAM HILL · TWICE F1 WORLD CHAMPION
heritage.Surtees: JOHN SURTEES · CHAMPION ON TWO AND FOUR WHEELS
heritage.McLaren: BRUCE MCLAREN · FOUNDER OF THE F1 TEAM
heritage.Westfield Bend: NAMED FOR WESTFIELD WOOD AROUND THE TRACK
heritage.Sheene Curve: BARRY SHEENE · TWICE MOTORCYCLE WORLD CHAMPION

tracks.story: Laid out in the parkland of Cadwell Hall in the Lincolnshire Wolds by Mansfield Wilkinson, with motorcycle races from 1934. Steep dips and crests earn it the name Britain's mini-Nurburgring.

heritage.Charlies: NAMED FOR A WILKINSON FAMILY MEMBER
heritage.Chris Curve: NAMED FOR A WILKINSON FAMILY MEMBER
heritage.The Mountain: BIKES GO AIRBORNE OVER THE MOUNTAIN
heritage.Hall Bends: THE OLD ENTRANCE ROAD TO CADWELL HALL
heritage.Barn: NAMED FOR A BARN, DEMOLISHED FOR RUN-OFF

tracks.story: Built in rolling sandhill country east of Toronto and opened in June 1961, when Stirling Moss won the first major race, the Player's 200. It hosted the Canadian Grand Prix in the 1960s and 70s and took the Canadian Tire name in 2012; fans still call it Mosport.

heritage.Moss Corner: STIRLING MOSS · WON THE FIRST BIG RACE

tracks.story: Opened in 1960 by Bruton Smith and Curtis Turner beside U.S. Route 29 in Concord, North Carolina. In 2018 the Roval joined the banked oval to the infield road course, the first road race in NASCAR Cup playoff history.

NASCAR's first street race wound through Grant Park, past Buckingham Fountain and along Lake Shore Drive. Shane van Gisbergen won the first Cup race in 2023 on his series debut, and the event ran through 2025.

Opened in Montmeló in September 1991 and on the F1 calendar the same year, Barcelona-Catalunya is the classic all-rounder: a long main straight, fast sweepers and slow corners, with a wind that can turn around during the day.
Built by Jean-Claude and Sylvie Bondurand in the hills above Lédenon, near Nîmes, and approved for racing in 1973. It runs anti-clockwise, rare in France, and climbs more than 34 metres in a lap.

heritage.La Cuvette: LOWEST POINT OF THE LAP, 173.78 M

tracks.story: Jean Bernigaud opened a kart track on his farmland in 1960, the Circuit Jean Behra. Rebuilt in 1989 with corners copied from tracks around the world, it hosted the French Grand Prix from 1991 to 2008, where Michael Schumacher won eight times.

heritage.Estoril: ESTORIL · AFTER THE PORTUGUESE GP TRACK
heritage.Adelaide: ADELAIDE · AFTER THE AUSTRALIAN GP TRACK
heritage.Château d'Eau: CHATEAU D'EAU · TOP OF THE PLATEAU

tracks.story: Laid out in 1921 on public roads linking Francorchamps, Malmedy and Stavelot, Spa ran its first 24 Hours in 1924. Its corners are named for Ardennes springs, fens, farms and Belgian heroes, and the weather can be dry at one end and wet at the other.

heritage.La Source: LA SOURCE · FOR THE SPRINGS OF SPA
heritage.Jacky Ickx Corner: JACKY ICKX · MULTIPLE LE MANS WINNER
heritage.Pouhon: POUHON · WHERE THE MINERAL WATER SPRINGS
heritage.Stavelot: STAVELOT · ON THE OLD ROAD CIRCUIT
heritage.Blanchimont: BLANCHIMONT · FLAT OUT TO THE CHICANE
heritage.Bus Stop: THERE REALLY WAS A BUS STOP HERE

tracks.story: Laid out on Île Notre-Dame, the man-made island raised for Expo 67, beside the 1976 Olympic rowing basin. Local hero Gilles Villeneuve won the first Grand Prix here in 1978, and the circuit took his name in 1982.

heritage.Virage Senna: NAMED IN HONOUR OF AYRTON SENNA
heritage.Wall of Champions: 1999: HILL, SCHUMACHER, VILLENEUVE ALL HIT IT

tracks.story: Opened in October 2012 outside Austin and laid out with help from Hermann Tilke, COTA borrows corners from Silverstone, Hockenheim and Istanbul. The lap starts with a climb of over 11 percent to Turn 1, Big Red, the highest point. A 251-foot observation tower stands over the stadium section.

heritage.Big Red: FOR RED MCCOMBS · AN EARLY COTA INVESTOR

tracks.story: Built after the Second World War on roads laid by the German occupiers, in the dunes beside the North Sea. The first race ran in August 1948, and the 2020 rebuild added steep banking at Hugenholtz and the final Luyendyk corner.

heritage.Tarzanbocht: LEGEND SAYS: A LOCAL MAN NICKNAMED TARZAN
heritage.Scheivlak: OLD DUTCH FOR BORDER · AN OLD DUNE BOUNDARY

tracks.story: Opened on 8 December 1985 near Jerez de la Frontera, it held the Spanish Grand Prix in April 1986. Since 2018 it carries the name of Ángel Nieto, and seven of its corners honour motorcycle riders.

heritage.Curva Ángel Nieto: ANGEL NIETO · THE CIRCUIT BEARS HIS NAME

tracks.story: Opened near Los Arcos in northern Spain in June 2010, Navarra has hosted Superleague Formula, FIA GT1 and World Superbike. MotorSport Vision rebuilt and extended it in 2024.

Bill France Sr.'s 'World Center of Racing' opened in February 1959 with the first Daytona 500. Its road course links the infield to the 31-degree banking, and the sports car race there has run to 24 hours since 1966.

heritage.Bus Stop: REBUILT IN A BUS STOP SHAPE IN 1984-85

tracks.story: Fred Craner laid out Donington on the roads of a country estate in 1931, and by 1937 the Mercedes-Benz and Auto Union teams were racing here. After the war it became an army vehicle depot until Tom Wheatcroft bought it and reopened it in 1977; in 1993 Ayrton Senna won the rain-soaked European Grand Prix here.

heritage.Redgate: BY THE OLD ESTATE'S REDGATE LODGE
heritage.Hollywood: ONCE THE HOLLY WOOD ON THE ESTATE
heritage.Craner Curves: FRED CRANER · FATHER OF DONINGTON RACING
heritage.Schwantz Curve: FOR GRAND PRIX RIDER KEVIN SCHWANTZ
heritage.Coppice: NAMED FOR THE LOST COPPICE WOOD

tracks.story: Opened in 1966 in the eastern foothills of Mount Fuji, the circuit hosted Japan's first Formula 1 race in 1976. Toyota bought it in 2000 and rebuilt it for 2005. Its 1.475 km straight is one of the longest in racing, and rain and mist often visit.

Born in 1932 as a 12 km triangle through the forest, Hockenheim grew its famous Motodrom stadium in 1966 and hosted the German Grand Prix from 1977. Hermann Tilke's 2002 redesign cut the forest straights for the Parabolika and the Spitzkehre hairpin, but the stadium finish, ringed by grandstands, still decides races.

heritage.Turn 2: JIM CLARK MEMORIAL STANDS OUTSIDE TURN 2
heritage.Mercedes: IN FRONT OF THE MERCEDES-BENZ STAND
heritage.Parabolika: THE 2002 STRAIGHT THAT REPLACED THE FOREST

tracks.story: Ralph Sanchez built Homestead as the town recovered from Hurricane Andrew, opening it in November 1995. Rebuilt from a rectangle to an oval in 1997, it gained variable banking up to 20 degrees in 2003. Its infield road courses hosted Trans-Am, FIA GT and Grand-Am.

Built in eight months in a valley outside Budapest, the Hungaroring hosted the first Formula 1 race behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. For its 40th anniversary in 2026 every corner was named, for legends from Piquet to Senna and for Hungary itself.

heritage.Piquet: NELSON PIQUET · WON THE FIRST TWO HERE
heritage.Spring: THE VALLEY OF THE THREE SPRINGS
heritage.Buda: BUDA · ONE HALF OF THE CAPITAL
heritage.Pest: PEST · THE OTHER HALF OF BUDAPEST
heritage.Alesi: JEAN ALESI · A FAN NAME SINCE 1995
heritage.Senna: AYRTON SENNA · FIRST POLE HERE IN 1986
heritage.Szisz: FERENC SZISZ · WON THE FIRST GP IN 1906

tracks.story: The Brickyard opened in 1909 and has run the Indianapolis 500 since 1911. Its road course winds through the infield and uses the famous front straight, where a yard of original bricks still marks the line.

heritage.Main straight: A YARD OF 1909 BRICKS STILL MARKS THE LINE

tracks.story: Opened on 15 September 2006 in Newton, about 35 miles east of Des Moines, with Rusty Wallace as lead designer. Its 1.3-mile road course was built with the oval, using most of it plus a tight infield section.
Opened on 2 June 2001 in Kansas City, Kansas. A road course was added in 2012 with the repave, mixing the oval with a twisty infield, and Grand-Am's Rolex Sports Car Series raced it in 2013 and 2014.

Knockhill opened in 1974 on Fife farmland, stitched together from farm service roads and a disused colliery railway. Scotland's only FIA-licensed circuit, it became the first modern UK track licensed to race both ways.

heritage.Leslie's: NAMED IN 2008 FOR RACER DAVID LESLIE
heritage.Hislop's: BUILT ON A DISUSED COLLIERY RAILWAY
heritage.Railway straight: FOLLOWS THE OLD LETHANS COLLIERY LINE

tracks.story: Built in 1957 around a dry lake bed on former Fort Ord army land near Monterey; Laguna Seca is Spanish for dry lake. Its signature is the Corkscrew, a blind 59-foot drop.

heritage.Andretti Hairpin: FOR MARIO ANDRETTI · F1 WORLD CHAMPION
heritage.The Corkscrew: A 59-FOOT PLUNGE OFF A BLIND CREST
heritage.Rahal Straight: FOR BOBBY RAHAL · CHAMP CAR RACE WINNER

tracks.story: Opened in 1987 near the village of Hell as Norway's first asphalt track, owned by the Norwegian Automobile Federation. Built on a hillside with big elevation changes, it has hosted European Rallycross since 2011 and World RX from 2014, sold as 'Rallycross in Hell'.

The 'Diamond in the Desert' opened its 1.5-mile oval in 1996 with an IndyCar race won by Richie Hearn. Two road courses sit in the infield and a third uses the big oval, with banking raised to 20 degrees in 2006.

Opened in April 1957 in the Connecticut hills, built by Jim Vaill with help from John Fitch. A 1959 court injunction still bans Sunday racing. There are no grandstands: fans sit on grassy hillsides under the trees, and straights now honour Sam Posey and Paul Newman.

heritage.Big Bend: MORE THAN 180 DEGREES ACROSS TWO CORNERS
heritage.The Left-Hander: THE ONLY LEFT ON THE CLASSIC LAP
heritage.The Right-Hander: NAMED BECAUSE IT FOLLOWS THE LEFT-HANDER
heritage.The Downhill: FASTEST CORNER · BEGINS AT THE BAILEY BRIDGE
heritage.The Uphill: A BLIND CREST WITH LITTLE RUNOFF
heritage.Paul Newman Straight: THE OLD NO NAME STRAIGHT · FOR PAUL NEWMAN

tracks.story: Promoter Chris Pook brought racing to the streets of Long Beach in 1975, and Formula One followed as the United States Grand Prix West from 1976 to 1983. Today's 11-turn layout, in use since 2000, wraps around the Convention Center, from the palm-lined Shoreline Drive to the Fountain and the final hairpin.

Laid out through the grounds of Hard Rock Stadium, home of the Miami Dolphins, the Autodrome joined Formula 1 in 2022. Nineteen turns, three long straights and a twisting section that climbs over a ramp and under the flyovers.

heritage.Back straight: THE LONGEST STRAIGHT ISN'T THE PIT STRAIGHT

tracks.story: Les Griebling and Mansfield-area businessmen built Mid-Ohio in 1962 for weekend sports car racing. Jim Trueman, founder of Red Roof Inns, modernized it from 1982; iRacing rebuilt it for 2026.

heritage.The Esses: THE ESSES · UPHILL, OVER, AND DOWN
heritage.The Chicane: BYPASSED SINCE 1990 BY MOST PRO SERIES

tracks.story: The oldest operating motor speedway in the world, racing at Wisconsin State Fair Park since 1903. The infield road course dates from the 1954 paving, and iRacing's 2026 re-scan added a road layout to the oval.
Opened in 1972 as the Santamonica circuit near Rimini, Misano was lengthened and turned to run clockwise in 2006. Since 2012 it has carried the name of Marco Simoncelli.

Honda built it in 1997 to bring CART racing to Japan, a road course and an oval side by side, hence Twin Ring Motegi. Renamed Mobility Resort Motegi for its 25th anniversary in 2022; demolition of the oval began in May 2026.

Designed by Hermann Tilke with Foster and Partners, MotorLand Aragón opened at Alcañiz in September 2009. Corners honour Spanish champions Carlos Checa and Marc Márquez; the National layout is 2.6 km.

Built on a former maize field west of Magdeburg and opened in July 1997 as Motopark Oschersleben, Germany's fourth permanent circuit. Renamed Motorsport Arena Oschersleben in 2005, it has hosted DTM, FIA GT and World Superbike. In 2007 Turn 1 was reshaped into a sharp 90-degree left to create overtaking.

heritage.Triple Curves: THE TRIPLE LEFT · THE CAR GOES LIGHT

tracks.story: Opened in 1938 on Mount Panorama above Bathurst. Up Mountain Straight, across the top at 862 metres, down through the Esses, then Conrod Straight, where Supercars touch 300 km/h.

heritage.Hell Corner: NAMED FOR A TREE STUMP ON THE APEX
heritage.Griffins Bend: MAYOR MARTIN GRIFFIN · HIS VISION, THIS TRACK
heritage.The Cutting: CUT INTO THE ROCK OF THE MOUNTAIN
heritage.Quarry Corner: THE QUARRY BELOW ITS OUTSIDE WALL
heritage.McPhillamy Park: WALTER MCPHILLAMY · GAVE THE LAND TO THE CITY
heritage.The Dipper: A DIP THAT ONCE LIFTED CARS ONTO TWO WHEELS
heritage.Forrest's Elbow: JACK FORREST GROUND HIS ELBOW HERE IN 1947
heritage.The Chase: ADDED IN 1987 TO BREAK UP CONROD
heritage.Mountain Straight: A 1.1 KM CLIMB UP THE MOUNT
heritage.Conrod Straight: NAMED FOR KLEINIG'S BROKEN CONROD IN 1939

tracks.story: The Magic Mile grew out of Bryar Motorsports Park, a 1965 road course for motorcycles. Bob Bahre bought it in 1989 and built the paper-clip oval; the road course mixes the oval with twisting infield roads.

tracks.display: New Jersey Motorsports Park - Thunderbolt Raceway
tracks.story: Thunderbolt Raceway opened in 2008 beside Millville airport, a former Army Air Corps fighter training field. The circuit is named for the P-47 Thunderbolt that trained there, and its toughest section is the Jersey Devil.

Opened in June 1927 in the Eifel hills, the Nordschleife winds through forest and villages for more than 20 km. Jackie Stewart called it the Green Hell after winning the 1968 German Grand Prix in rain and fog. The combined lap links the modern GP circuit to the old loop for the NLS races and the 24 Hours.

heritage.Sabine-Schmitz-Kurve: FOR SABINE SCHMITZ · FACE OF THE GREEN HELL
heritage.Hatzenbach: NAMED FOR THE STREAM BESIDE THE TRACK
heritage.Quiddelbacher Höhe: NAMED FOR THE VILLAGE OF QUIDDELBACH
heritage.Flugplatz: A SMALL AIRFIELD STOOD HERE EARLY ON
heritage.Aremberg: NAMED FOR AREMBERG VILLAGE AND CASTLE
heritage.Fuchsröhre: A FOX HID IN A DRAIN PIPE DURING THE BUILD
heritage.Miss-Hit-Miss: MISS, HIT, MISS · THE LINE IS THE NAME
heritage.Bergwerk: NAMED FOR AN OLD LEAD AND SILVER MINE
heritage.Hohe Acht: NAMED FOR THE NEARBY HOHE ACHT MOUNTAIN
heritage.Hedwigshöhe: FOR HEDWIG, WIFE OF DESIGNER OTTO CREUTZ
heritage.Eiskurve: ICE CORNER · BLACK ICE HERE IN WINTER
heritage.Pflanzgarten: ONCE THE GARDENS OF THE COUNTS OF NURBURG
heritage.Pflanzgarten II: ONCE THE GARDENS OF THE COUNTS OF NURBURG
heritage.Antoniusbuche: NAMED FOR A GREAT BEECH TREE
heritage.Yokohama-S: NAMED BY THE TYRE MAKER FROM 2008
heritage.Döttinger Höhe: ONE OF EUROPE'S LONGEST FLAT-OUT RUNS

tracks.story: Built in 1982-84 on the old Nordschleife pit site and Südschleife. Revamped in 2002 with the Haug hook and Mercedes Arena; its corners carry sponsors' names and one for Michael Schumacher.

heritage.Haug-Haken: THE HAUG HOOK · REPLACED THE 2002 CHICANE
heritage.ADVAN-Bogen: ADVAN BOGEN · ON THE BACK STRAIGHT
heritage.Yokohama-S: NAMED BY THE TYRE MAKER FROM 2008

tracks.story: Opened in June 1927 through the Eifel hills, 20.8 km and officially 73 corners. Lauda's 1976 crash ended its Grand Prix era; today it is the home of the 24 Hours and the Industriefahrten lap.

heritage.Wehrseifen: WEHRSEIFEN · VALLEY ON THE OLD BORDER
heritage.Breidscheid: BREIDSCHEID · LOWEST POINT OF THE LAP
heritage.Bergwerk: BERGWERK · AN OLD LEAD AND SILVER MINE
heritage.Hohe Acht: HOHE ACHT · ONE OF THE HIGHEST POINTS

tracks.story: Opened in 1990 as TI Circuit Aida, a members' club track built by golf-course owner Hajime Tanaka in the hills of Okayama. It hosted Formula One's Pacific Grand Prix in 1994 and 1995, both won by Michael Schumacher, and most of its corners honour the veteran British drivers who raced at its first members' event.

heritage.Back Straight: FASTEST PART OF THE LAP · ABOUT 700 M

tracks.story: Opened in 1962 on grazing land south-west of Sydney, Oran Park grew in 1974 into a figure-eight with a bridge where the track crosses itself. It hosted the Australian Grand Prix in 1974 and 1977 and decades of touring car racing. It closed in 2010 for housing; iRacing scanned it just before demolition.

Laid out through the parkland of the Egerton family's Oulton estate in Cheshire, where US troops camped before D-Day. Racing began in 1953, and in 1961 Stirling Moss won the Gold Cup here in the four-wheel-drive Ferguson.

heritage.Old Hall: NAMED FOR OULTON HALL, BURNED DOWN IN 1926
heritage.Foster's: FOR LONG-TIME CIRCUIT MANAGER RAY FOSTER
heritage.Knickerbrook: BLASTER BATES TALE GAVE THIS CORNER ITS NAME
heritage.Lodge: NAMED FOR THE ESTATE GATEHOUSE, STILL STANDING
heritage.Deer Leap: JOE LOUIS BOXED FOR TROOPS HERE IN WWII
heritage.Britten's Chicane: FOR OWNERS JOHN FOULSTON AND JOHN BRITTEN
heritage.Hill Top: THE HIGHEST POINT OF THE CIRCUIT

tracks.story: Racing began on the island's roads in 1928 with what became the first Australian Grand Prix. The current circuit opened in 1952 and reopened in 1988; its corners honour Doohan, Stoner, Miller and Len Lukey.

heritage.Stoner Corner: CASEY STONER · SIX STRAIGHT HOME WINS
heritage.Lukey Heights: LEN LUKEY · BOUGHT AND SAVED THE TRACK

tracks.story: Phoenix International Raceway opened in 1964 in the Estrella Mountains west of Phoenix, built with a road course first and the one-mile oval added at promoter J. C. Agajanian's urging. iRacing's 2008 version keeps the pre-2011 oval with its trademark backstretch dogleg and the 1.51-mile infield road course that hosted sports cars from 2000 to 2006.

The Tricky Triangle in the Pocono Mountains: three corners, each modelled on another track - Trenton, Indianapolis and the Milwaukee Mile. The 2.5-mile tri-oval opened in 1971, and its infield road courses can run either direction since a 2013 rebuild.

heritage.Tunnel Turn: THE TUNNEL TURN · MODELLED ON INDIANAPOLIS

tracks.story: Portland races on the streets of Vanport, a city wiped out by the Columbia River flood of May 1948. Racing began here in 1961 with the Rose Festival, and the hard Shelton Chicane at the end of the front straight funnels the field at the start of every lap.

heritage.Main straight: ON THE REMAINS OF COTTONWOOD STREET

tracks.story: A 3.4-mile street course on Naval Air Station North Island, designed by iRacing for NASCAR's 2026 return to Southern California. It runs past the aircraft carrier pier at Carrier Corner and out along a runway. Corey Heim won the first Cup race here in June 2026.

Opened in 1969 as the Österreichring in the Styrian hills, it was rebuilt by Hermann Tilke as the A1-Ring in 1996. Red Bull reopened it as the Red Bull Ring in 2011, and Turn 1 now honours Niki Lauda.
Clif Tufte opened Road America in 1955 after Elkhart Lake's open-road races were stopped. Four miles through Wisconsin's Kettle Moraine, still in its original layout, with the Kink and Canada Corner.

heritage.The Kink: THE KINK · FLAT OUT, NO RUNOFF
heritage.Kettle Bottoms: KETTLE BOTTOMS · WALLS AND NO RUNOFF
heritage.Thunder Valley: THUNDER VALLEY · THE SOUND HANGS HERE
heritage.Bill Mitchell Bend: BILL MITCHELL · THE OLD BRIDGE AT T13

tracks.story: Built on 750 acres of Georgia farmland and opened in 1970 with a Can-Am race. Home of Petit Le Mans since 1998, a 2.54-mile hill-and-dale lap that ends by diving off the crest into Turn 12.

heritage.The Esses: DOWNHILL THEN UPHILL THROUGH THE ESSES
heritage.Turn 10: ADDED IN 1996, ENDED THE OLD DIP
heritage.Turn 12: OVER THE EDGE AND DOWN TO THE LINE
heritage.Back straight: ONE MILE FROM TURN 7, OVER THE HILL

tracks.story: Opened in October 1965 in Rockingham, North Carolina; Curtis Turner won the first race, the American 500. NASCAR left in 2004, came back briefly in 2012-13, and returned again in 2025.

Norway's oldest asphalt circuit, opened on 20 May 1990 with Thierry Boutsen cutting the ribbon. Hermann Tilke redesigned it as the national motorsport centre and it reopened in 2012, cut through pine forest and rock with 42 metres of elevation.

First raced in 1927 on public roads through Hohenstein-Ernstthal and named Sachsenring in 1937. The road course closed in 1990; the short permanent circuit opened in 1996 and hosts the German motorcycle Grand Prix.

heritage.Omega: THE OMEGA · A LOOP AROUND A WOODED HILL

tracks.story: Sandown opened in March 1962 with Jack Brabham, Jim Clark and Stirling Moss on the grid, laid around a horse-racing course in Melbourne's south-east. Its two drag-strip straights and the fast esses made it home of the Sandown 500, Australia's traditional warm-up for Bathurst.

Laid out on Hendricks Field, a World War II training base for B-17 crews, with stretches of the old concrete runways still in the lap. The first race ran on New Year's Eve 1950, the first 12 Hours in 1952.

Built on RAF Silverstone, a wartime bomber station. It held the British Grand Prix in 1948 and in 1950 the first World Championship race; its corners are named for the abbey, chapel, farm and woods around it.

heritage.Bridge: NAMED FOR THE BRIDGE ACROSS THE TRACK

tracks.story: A wartime airfield used by the US 96th Bomb Group, turned into a circuit in 1951. MSV's 2011 rebuild added Jonathan Palmer's 300 layout, with corners named for racing greats and Norfolk heroes.

heritage.Riches: FRED RICHES · FARMER WHO SAVED THE SITE
heritage.Wilson: JUSTIN WILSON · RENAMED IN HIS HONOUR
heritage.Agostini: GIACOMO AGOSTINI · WON HERE ON TWO WHEELS
heritage.Hamilton: LEWIS HAMILTON · RACED HERE EARLY ON
heritage.Williams: SIR FRANK WILLIAMS · F1 TEAM FOUNDER
heritage.Bomb Hole: BOMB HOLE · A NICKNAME FOR THE DIP

tracks.story: Built in 1968 as Sears Point Raceway on a former dairy farm in the Sonoma wine-country hills. The long course climbs and drops through the Carousel, the signature corner the Cup cars returned to in 2019.
Racing on the St. Petersburg waterfront dates to 1985, when Trans-Am came downtown. IndyCars arrived in 2003 and the race often opens the season, with an airport runway as its front straight.

Designed and built in 1969-70 by local racing businessman Pat Goodman in West Virginia's Eastern Panhandle, two hours west of Washington. Bill Scott, the 1970 Formula Vee world champion, later co-owned it, and federal security agencies train here.
Honda's own circuit, designed by John Hugenholtz as a test track and opened in 1962. A figure of eight: the back straight crosses over the front half of the lap on a bridge.

Opened in 1996 in Fort Worth; its infield road course was finished in August 2000, when the American Le Mans Series raced a roval there. iRacing's road layouts are on the 2009 legacy scan, before the 2017 repave.

tracks.display: Shell V-Power Motorsport Park at The Bend
tracks.story: Built by Peregrine Corporation on the former Mitsubishi test track at Tailem Bend, about 100 km south-east of Adelaide, The Bend opened in January 2018 as Australia's first brand-new national-standard circuit in two decades. Its GT Circuit runs 7.77 km and 35 turns, and since 2023 Shell V-Power holds the naming rights.

Built in wartime as RAF Thruxton, the airfield first hosted motorcycle racing in 1950. Today's circuit opened in 1968 on the old perimeter road and is billed as the fastest in the UK; Damon Hill lapped it in 57.6s in a Williams FW15C in 1993.

heritage.Church: ONCE THE QUICKEST CORNER IN BRITAIN

tracks.story: Planned from 1966 to bring young people into motorsport, it opened on 22 June 1970, about 60 km north of Tokyo. Its short, flat lap is a benchmark: in 2023 a tuner car on street semi-slicks broke 50 seconds for the first time.

Built with a bulldozer on rolling farmland near Alton, Virginia, VIR opened in 1957. It closed in 1974 and came back to life in 2000; the oak that gave Oak Tree its name stood before the track was built and fell in 2013.

heritage.NASCAR Bend: PETTY, PEARSON AND SCOTT WENT OFF HERE, 1966
heritage.Oak Tree: AN OAK OLDER THAN THE TRACK, FELL IN 2013

tracks.story: Racing began on the village streets of Watkins Glen in 1948, and the permanent circuit opened in 1956. The Glen hosted the United States Grand Prix for twenty straight years, from 1961 to 1980.

tracks.story: Opened in November 1953, Willow Springs is billed as the oldest permanent road course in America. Ken Miles helped plan Big Willow, the 2.5-mile 'Fastest Road in the West', still in its 1953 layout.
Built by the Benalla Auto Club, Winton held its first meeting in November 1961. The 1997 extension created today's National Circuit, and touring cars have raced here since the 1985 ATCC round.

Born as a drag strip in 1967 and nicknamed 'The Swamp', the site east of St. Louis gained its oval in 1997. Closed in 2010 and revived by Curtis Francois, it took the World Wide Technology name in 2019 and joined the Cup schedule in 2022.
Built in woodland beside the canal outside Zolder, the extended Omloop Terlaemen opened in June 1963. It hosted Formula 1's Belgian Grand Prix between 1973 and 1984.
